full_judgment:
3. Mr Farooqui, at the very outset, has submitted that the respondent No. 1 was defendant No. 3 in Title Suit No. 181/90 which was a suit for foreclosure and was decreed and execution case has already been started. By referring to the decree of the suit, Annexure B (1), he has argued that the defendants mortgaged some property and took loan from Sonali Bank and as the loan was not repaid, the Bank instituted the suit for foreclosure. Next, Mr Faroque referred to section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act and has argued that the respondent No. 1 was a mortgagor and as a decree has already been passed against him for foreclosure, he is a defaulter within meaning of clause (a) of 2nd proviso to Article 12 of the Representation of the People Order, 1972. He has pointed out that under sub-section (MM) of section 5 of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 a defaulter has been defined and, according to him, respondent No.1 has also become a defaulter under that definition. Mr Farooqui has also submitted that the judgment was passed against the respondent No. 1 on 4-6-95, the execution case was started in 1997 but suppressing those facts, respondent No. 1 contested in the last general election from constituency No.132 Barisal with Pirojpur. So, according to him, as the respondent No.1 was a defaulter, his participation in the election was illegal and though he was elected he cannot hold that post. 

 6. Before we decide the questions raised in this writ petition, we like to consider whether this writ petition was filed actually to get relief which one may seek in a writ of quo warranto. Specific allegation of the respondent No. 1 is that the present writ petition has been filed only to cause harassment to the respondent No. 1. The present petition is filed by Mr Obaidullah Raihan. It has been categorically claimed that this writ petitioner was Assistant Private Secretary to Mr AK Faezul Huq who was State Minister for Jute and Textile. In the affidavit in reply on behalf of the respondent No. 1 a letter of the present petitioner as APS to the State Minister for Jute and Textile has been annexed (Anexure 4). This claim of the respondent No.1 that the present petitioner was APS to Mr AK Faezul Huq has not been denied. So, it is clear that the election petition has been filed by Mr AK Faezul Huq and the present petition has been filed by his former APS. Though in the writ petition itself the petitioner claims that he is a citizen of Bangladesh and hails from District Barisal and a voter in that Constituency No.132 Barisal, Pirojpur. At paragraph 4 of the writ petition it is mentioned that the respondent No. 1 was disqualified to contest in the election as Member of Parliament on the date of filing of nomination paper because the respondent No.5 Sonali Bank obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 181/90 against the respondent No.1 and two others and decretal amount still remained unrealised and as he was a defaulter, he was disqualified from being elected a Member of Parliament. Now, from the copy of the election petition No. 14 of 2001 which was filed by AK Faezul Huq, we find that in paragraph-3 of that Election Petition, it is also stated that respondent No.1 was not legally qualified for contesting the election as he was a loan defaulter because the Sonali Bank filed a Title Suit No. 181/90 for foreclosure against him and two others and obtained decree and for realisation of the decretal amount, the Bank already filed an execution case. In paragraph 5 of the Election Petition, it is also stated that at the time of filing of nomination paper on 29-8-2000, respondent was not qualified as the decretal amount still remained unrealised. It is also stated at paragraph 5 that the petitioner raised objection but Returning Officer did not consider his objection. From the Election Petition we find that the election has been challenged also on some other grounds. 

 8. Moreover, we have also taken into consideration the fact that the main grounds on which the election of the respondent No. 1 has been challenged in the Election Petition and in the present writ petition is, the ground of disqualification of respondent No. 1. In both the matters, disqualification is alleged, on the ground that Sonali Bank obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 181/90 against the respondent No. 1 and two others and though execution case was filed in 1997, the decretal amount remained unrealised on the date of filing of nomination paper by the respondent and, as such, he was a defaulter and disqualified under clause (a) of second provision to Article 12(1) of the Representation of the People Order, 1972. This question is to be decided in the Election Petition by the Bench of this Court constituted for the purpose. For the above reason we refrain from giving any finding on the question of disqualification and for the reason mentioned earlier, the Rule is liable to be struck out.
